answer: Require each agent to earn its place as a vertex in a verified work graph: before it can trade, it must complete small, peer-checked jobs that leave a public reputation signal. A single real agent builds that signal once, but an attacker creating thousands of fake identities must pay the full work cost for every one. That cost makes Sybil flooding unprofitable, while honest agents keep the useful services — the nectar of the network — flowing to participants who have actually proven themselves.
